### Subject: Opinion on arm's length pricing of intra-group management support fees under Section 92C

---

## 1. Purpose and Basis of this Opinion

This opinion is issued pursuant to our engagement letter dated [●], and is based solely on the facts and representations furnished by the management of Orion Consulting India Private Limited, and on the relevant provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, applicable rules, notifications, circulars, and judicial precedents as they stand on the date hereof. This opinion is addressed solely to, and for the sole use of, Orion Consulting India Private Limited for the specific purpose stated herein, and should not be relied upon, quoted, or disclosed to any third party without our prior written consent.

## 2. Statement of Facts

Orion Consulting India Private Limited pays its Singapore associated enterprise an annual fee of INR 12 crore, computed on a cost-plus 8% markup basis, for regional management support covering finance, HR, and IT functions. A Transactional Net Margin Method benchmarking study using six comparables indicates an arm's length markup range of 5% to 9%.

## 3. Issue for Consideration

Whether the management fee paid to the Singapore AE is at arm's length under Section 92C, and whether the benchmarking approach adopted is defensible.

## 4. Relevant Legal Framework

- Section 92
- Section 92C
- Section 92CA
- Rule 10B
- Rule 10CA


## 5. Judicial Precedents Considered

- CIT v. EKL Appliances Ltd, (2012) 345 ITR 241 (Del)
- Magneti Marelli Powertrain India (P) Ltd v. DCIT

## 6. Analysis

The 8% markup falls within the arm's length range of 5% to 9% derived from the comparable set, supporting the pricing under the TNMM. Following EKL Appliances, the tax authorities are not entitled to question the commercial expediency of the arrangement provided the services were genuinely rendered; however, Magneti Marelli underscores that contemporaneous documentation evidencing actual rendition and benefit derived (the 'benefit test') is essential to sustain the deduction and pricing on audit.

## 7. Conclusion / Opinion

The pricing of the management fee is at arm's length, provided the Company maintains robust, contemporaneous documentation evidencing the actual rendition of services and the benefit derived by the Company.

**Confidence level:** Reasonable / more likely than not, contingent on documentation
